obzhaya-informatsiya.title: General information
obzhaya-informatsiya.html:
Terms and definitions

  • System - the CloudPayments payment gateway.

  • Merchant - a business that uses the system.

  • API - a software interface for interacting with a system through https://api.cloudpayments.ru.

  • Dashboard - the merchant space in the system, available at https://merchant.cloudpayments.ru.

  • Card - a bank card issued by the Visa, Mastercard, or Mir payment system.

  • Acquirer - the settlement bank.

  • Issuer - the bank that issued the card.

  • Holder - a person to whom the issuer has issued a card for use.

  • Widget - a payment form provided by the system for the cardholder to enter card details and complete authorization.

  • 3D Secure - a protocol for verifying the cardholder's identity with the issuer.

Operation types

The system involves two types of transactions: payment and refund.

  • When the payment is made, the funds are transferred from the holder's account to the merchant. For a refund, the funds are transferred the other way around.

  • The merchant issues a refund if the customer wants to return the product.

  • The refund is always linked to a payment transaction, the amount of which is returned to the cardholder. Both the full payment and part of it can be refunded. The funds are usually returned to the cardholder's card on the same day, but sometimes, depending on the issuing bank, this can take up to 3 days.

  • Unlike a refund, a payment transaction can be canceled.

  • The merchant cancels a payment if it was made by mistake, for example, due to an incorrect amount or technical failure. There is one limitation: the transaction can only be canceled when using a two-stage payment scheme. At the same time, the funds will be released on the cardholder’s card almost instantly.

Payment processing methods

There are two ways to process payments: single-stage and two-stage, also known as the single message system (SMS) and dual message system (DMS), respectively.

Single-stage payment is processed with a single command, which authorizes and subsequently debits the funds to the merchant.

Two-stage payment uses two separate commands: one for authorization and one for charging the funds. After successful authorization, the transaction amount is held on the cardholder's account, so they cannot use the funds. Next, the merchant has up to 7 days, depending on the card type, to confirm the transaction, after which the funds are debited. If the operation is not confirmed within this period, it will be canceled automatically. You can confirm either full authorization amount or part of it.

As a rule, a two-stage method is used to collect a deposit from the payer, for example, by rental companies or hotels.

Depending on the configuration, the system can automatically confirm two-stage payments after the specified number of days.

Payment methods

Payment can be made in the following ways:

  • Through the payment form, the widget. You add a script to your website that opens a secure payment form, an iframe for entering card details.

  • Via the API using a card cryptogram. A checkout script is integrated into your website to collect card details from any form, encrypt and generate a cryptogram for secure server-to-server transmission.

  • Via the SDK for mobile apps. The mobile SDK is integrated into your iOS or Android app to accept card payments directly from your customers' smartphones or tablets.

  • Via the API using a card token: recurring payments. Following the first payment via the widget or by cryptogram, the system assigns a token to the card details. The token can be safely stored and used for merchant-initiated payments (one-click payments). The token is returned in the Pay notification and in the API response

  • Via a configured recurring payment plan. Following the first payment or a one-ruble authorization for card verification, a token is assigned to the card details. This token is then used to create a subscription plan for recurring payments. Payments are processed automatically by the system without the payer's confirmation. These payments follow a configured schedule, which can be set to once a day (or every few days), once a week (or every few weeks) or once a month (or every few months). If a scheduled payment attempt fails, a notification is sent, and the attempt is retried within a day. After three consecutive failed attempts, the subscription is automatically canceled. When creating a plan, a maximum number of billing cycles can be specified (for example, 12 months for a monthly subscription), after which the subscription will automatically terminate.

  • Customizable payment acceptance forms. Payment forms allow foundations and other organizations to accept donations directly to their accounts using a configurable, customizable payment form. This form can be shared as a link c.cloudpayments.ru/payments/ or as a QR code, which can be placed in both online broadcasts and offline marketing materials (flyers, brochures, etc.). The form makes it much easier to accept donations. In the new "Payment forms" section of the dashboard, you can create and customize up to 5 payment forms. The link and QR code for sending to payers become available once the form is saved.

3D Secure

3D Secure is the collective name for the security programs developed by Visa and Mastercard. The purpose of the program is to verify the identity of the cardholder, allowing the issuer to protect against unauthorized card use prior to payment. In practice, it works as follows: the cardholder enters their card details and is then redirected to the issuer's website to enter a password or verification code. Typically, the code is sent via SMS. If the code is entered correctly, the payment is processed. Otherwise, it is declined.

3D Secure is not triggered for all cards during checkout, but only for those whose issuing banks support the technology. Processing payments without 3D Secure is a less secure option.

platezhniy-widget.title: Payment widget
platezhniy-widget.html:
Payment widget is a pop-up form used to enter the payer's card details and email address. The widget automatically determines the type of payment network: Visa, Mastercard, Maestro, or Mir, as well as the issuing bank, and displays the corresponding logos. The form is optimized for all browsers and mobile devices. Inside the widget, an iframe opens that ensures the secure transmission of card details and does not require compliance certification from the merchant. _Widget

Detailed developer documentation: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/docs/widget.html

Demo of the payment form builder: https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/app/demo

Demo widget

A demonstration of how the Widget works is available in our demo store:

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited.


Widget installation

To install the widget, add the script to the head section of your website:

javascript
<script src="https://widget.cloudpayments.ru/bundles/cloudpayments.js"></script>

Warning: Use cloudpayments.js to maintain PCI compliance by ensuring that payment details are sent directly to CloudPayments without affecting your server. Always load cloudpayments.js from https://widget.cloudpayments.ru to remain compliant. Do not bundle the script or host it yourself. _Widget

To display the payment form, register a function to call the pay method by passing either the auth or the charge parameter to it:

json
this.pay = function () {
 var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    widget.pay('auth', // or 'charge'
        { //options
            publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000002', // ID from the dashboard
            description: 'Payment for goods at example.com', // Payment description
            amount: 100, // Amount
            currency: 'RUB', // Currency
            accountId: 'user@example.com', // Payer ID (optional)
            invoiceId: '1234567', // Order number (optional)
            email: 'user@example.com', // Payer email (optional)
            skin: "mini", // Widget design (optional)
            autoClose: 3, // Time in seconds before widget auto-close (optional)
            data: {
                myProp: 'myProp value'
            },
            configuration: {
                common: {
                    successRedirectUrl: "https://{your website}/success", // Redirection URL
                    failRedirectUrl: "https://{your website}/fail"        // If paid via T-Pay
                }
            },
            payer: {
                firstName: 'Test',
                lastName: 'Testov',
                middleName: 'Testovich',
                birth: '1955-02-24',
                address: 'test drive test home',
                street: 'Lenina',
                city: 'MO',
                country: 'RU',
                phone: '+71234567890',
                postcode: '345'
            }
        },
        {
            onSuccess: function (options) { // Success
                // Triggered on payment success
            },
            onFail: function (reason, options) { // Fail
                // Triggered on payment failure
            },
            onComplete: function (paymentResult, options) {
                // Triggered as soon as the widget receives a response
                // with transaction result from api.cloudpayments
                // For example, calling your analytics
            }
        }
    )
};

Then, call the function in response to an event, such as clicking the Pay button:

javascript
$('#checkout').click(pay);

Notice: The example uses the jQuery library.

A demonstration of how the widget works is available in our demo store:
https://show.cloudpayments.ru

Example of running the widget without jQuery:

javascript
document.querySelector('#checkout').onclick = pay

Embedded JSFiddle:

json
<script async src="//jsfiddle.net/tretyakovsky/xvec6jpb/35/embed/js,html/dark/"></script>

You can use both test card details and real ones for testing. No funds will be debited. _Widget

Parameters

Notice: According to the NSPK requirements, merchant platforms providing telecommunication services (MCC 4814 Telecommunication Services), must provide the payer's phone number. If the phone number is missing from the request, acquiring banks will decline the transactions.

The phone number must be passed in the Phone parameter within the Payer object.

Format: digits only, without delimiters such as hyphens or parentheses.

Example: +71234567890 _Widget

Calling the pay function with either the auth or the charge argument determines the payment processing method:

  • charge for single-stage payments

  • auth for two-stage payments

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

publicId

string

Yes

Website ID, can be found in the dashboard

amount

float

Yes

Payment amount

currency

string

Yes

Currency: RUB/USD/EUR/GBP

accountId

string

Required for subscription creation

User ID

description

string

No

Free-form description of the payment purpose

invoiceId

string

No

Order or invoice number

email

string

No

User's email

requireEmail

bool

No

Requirement to display the user email address field in the widget

data

JSON

No

Any other data associated with the transaction, including instructions for creating a subscription or generating an online receipt, must be wrapped in the cloudpayments object. Reserved parameter names: name, firstName, middleName, lastName, nick, phone, address, comment, birthDate

skin

string

No

Widget design selection. Possible options: classic, modern, mini. Default is classic

retryPayment

bool

No

Displays the "Retry payment" button upon a failed transaction. Default is true

autoClose

number

No

Automatically closes the widget after successful payment following a specified number of seconds, from 3 to 10

payer

object

No

Additional field used to pass payer information: firstName, lastName, middleName, birth, street, address, city, country, phone, postcode

configuration.common.successRedirectUrl

string

No

Redirect URL after a successful non-card payment. For SBP, the value must not exceed 1024 characters, use ASCII encoding, and comply with RFC-3986

configuration.common.failRedirectUrl

string

No

Redirect URL after a failed T-Pay payment

disableEmail

bool

No

Allows hiding the email address field. To hide it, omit requireEmail or set it to false

You can configure the form's behavior for successful or failed payments using the following parameters:

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

onSuccess

Function or String

No

Specify either a function or a website URL. If a function is specified, it will be called after the payment is successfully completed and the user closes the widget. If a URL is specified, the user will be redirected to that page

onFail

Function or String

No

Specify either a function or a website URL. If a function is specified, it will be called after a failed payment. If a URL is specified, the user will be redirected to that page

onComplete

Function

No

Specify a function to be triggered as soon as the widget receives the transaction result response. Redirects are not allowed in this method

Widget language settings

By default, the widget is displayed in Russian. To display the widget in another language, pass the language parameter in the widget initialization settings.

javascript
var widget = new cp.CloudPayments({language: "en-US"});

List of supported languages:

Language

Timezone

Code

Russian

MSK

ru-RU

English

CET

en-US

Kazakh

ALMT

kk-KZ

Recurring payments (subscriptions)

After the payment is successfully completed, the widget can automatically create a subscription for recurring payments. To do this, add several initialization parameters:

Parameter

Format

Required

Description

Interval

string

Yes

Interval. Possible values: Day, Week, Month

Period

int

Yes

Period. Combined with interval, 1 Month is once a month, and 2 Week is once every two weeks. Must be greater than 0

MaxPeriods

int

No

Maximum number of payments in subscription. By default, no restrictions. If you specify a number, make sure it is greater than 0

Amount

number

No

Recurring payment amount. By default, this matches the initial payment amount. If specifying a custom amount, ensure it is greater than 0

StartDate

DateTime

No

Date and time of the first recurring payment. By default, the next payment will occur after the specified interval and period. If specifying a custom date, ensure it is set in the future

CustomerReceipt

string

No

Data for online receipts generation in recurring payments

The parameters for launching recurring payments must be added to the data.CloudPayments.recurrent object, as shown in the example below:

json
this.pay = function () {
    var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    var receipt = {
        Items: [// Receipt items
            {
                label: 'Product name 3', // Product name
                price: 300.00, // Cost
                quantity: 3.00, // Quantity
                amount: 900.00, // Amount
                vat: 20, // VAT rate
                method: 0, // Tag 1214: payment method flag
                object: 0, // Tag 1212: payment subject flag
            }
        ],
        taxationSystem: 0,
        email: 'user@example.com',
        phone: '+71234567890',
        isBso: false,
        amounts: {
            electronic: 900.00,
            advancePayment: 0.00,
            credit: 0.00,
            provision: 0.00
        }
    };

    var data = {};
    data.CloudPayments = {
        CustomerReceipt: receipt,
        recurrent: {
            interval: 'Month',
            period: 1,
            customerReceipt: receipt
        }
    };

    widget.charge({
        publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000001',
        description: 'Monthly subscription for access to example.com',
        amount: 1000,
        currency: 'RUB',
        invoiceId: '1234567',
        accountId: 'user@example.com',
        data: data
    },
    function (options) {
        // Triggered on payment success
    },
    function (reason, options) {
        // Triggered on payment failure
    });
};

Please note that you can create a subscription by specifying the accountId parameter, which can be an email address, a phone number, or any other payer ID.

For more examples of creating recurring payments from the widget, see the Integration scenarios.

To cancel recurring payments, use the merchant dashboard, the API, or provide the customer with a link to the system's website:

https://my.cloudpayments.ru/

There they can find and cancel their subscriptions independently. _Widget

Mobile widget

The script automatically identifies the user's device and launches the most appropriate widget: desktop or mobile. For the convenience of customers, the mobile version of the widget opens in full screen, allowing them to pay either by card or via one of the alternative payment methods.

Parameter

Format

Required

Maximum number of payments in subscription. By default, no restrictions. If you specify a number, make sure it is greater than 0

Recurring payment amount. By default, this matches the initial payment amount. If specifying a custom amount, ensure it is greater than 0

The parameters for launching recurring payments must be added to the data.CloudPayments.recurrent object, as shown in the example below:

json
this.pay = function () {
    var widget = new cp.CloudPayments();
    var receipt = {
        Items: [// Receipt items
            {
                label: 'Product name 3', // Product name
                price: 300.00, // Cost
                quantity: 3.00, // Quantity
                amount: 900.00, // Amount
                vat: 20, // VAT rate
                method: 0, // Tag 1214: payment method flag
                object: 0, // Tag 1212: payment subject flag
            }
        ],
        taxationSystem: 0,
        email: 'user@example.com',
        phone: '+71234567890',
        isBso: false,
        amounts: {
            electronic: 900.00,
            advancePayment: 0.00,
            credit: 0.00,
            provision: 0.00
        }
    };

    var data = {};
    data.CloudPayments = {
        CustomerReceipt: receipt,
        recurrent: {
            interval: 'Month',
            period: 1,
            customerReceipt: receipt
        }
    };

    widget.charge({
        publicId: 'test_api_00000000000000000000001',
        description: 'Monthly subscription for access to example.com',
        amount: 1000,
        currency: 'RUB',
        invoiceId: '1234567',
        accountId: 'user@example.com',
        data: data
    },
    function (options) {
        // Triggered on payment success
    },
    function (reason, options) {
        // Triggered on payment failure
    });
};

Please note that you can create a subscription by specifying the accountId parameter, which can be an email address, a phone number, or any other payer ID.

For more examples of creating recurring payments from the widget, see the Integration scenarios.

To cancel recurring payments, use the merchant dashboard, the API, or provide the customer with a link to the system's website:

https://my.cloudpayments.ru/

There they can find and cancel their subscriptions independently. _Widget
